changes.why: enforceNoDualTypeDependencies (no package in both dependencies and devDependencies) is a disjoint-dependency-fields assertion. Caveat: the rule exempts a dependencies range containing "condition:", which reads the value and could argue B-adapter, but there are 0 condition: specifiers at the pin, so the key-only form is the enforced behavior.
The exemption reads the value: a dependencies range that uses condition: may repeat in devDependencies (yarn.config.cjs:159-173), and .yarnrc.yml declares the BABEL_9_BREAKING condition.
The alint field still named Stage A's set form; the integrator and the audit settled on unique-key with entry values.

It is not code analysis: the script only applies a regex to the file text. file_content_matches expresses it exactly. R4: my probe rule passed on the clone and on a clean scratch copy, and fired 1 when the annotation was stripped from typeof.ts.
units.fire_verified: n/a (family other). Still verified: the probe passed on the clone and a clean copy, and fired 1 on a copy with the @minVersion line removed from src/helpers/typeof.ts.

changes.why: The alint text gave a proposed or scratch rule id; the rule is in the configuration.

units.summary: Every non-syntax, non-modules plugin key in preset-env's available-plugins map is a key of @babel/compat-data's plugins.json or plugin-bugfixes.json.
units.evidence: packages/babel-preset-env/test/index.skip-bundled.js:38-59, the test "available-plugins is in sync with @babel/compat-data" (jest in the ci.yml test jobs). It takes the keys of src/available-plugins.ts (62 keys), excluding syntax-*, transform-modules-* and transform-dynamic-import, and requires each to be a key of packages/babel-compat-data/data/plugins.json or plugin-bugfixes.json. Three bugfix keys exist only in plugins.json, so the union is required.
units.alint: cross_file superset: the source set is files packages/babel-compat-data/data/{plugins,plugin-bugfixes}.json with regex (?m)^  "([^"]+)": \{; four targets over packages/babel-preset-env/src/available-plugins.ts with complement regexes (bugfix/..., transform-[^dm"]..., transform-d minus dynamic-import, transform-m minus modules-) to emulate the prefix exclusions.
units.reason: A set inclusion between two named key sets, expressible today but only by reading JSON keys and TS object keys with layout-specific regexes plus hand-written complement patterns for the exclusions. The batch-2 ruling makes a regex read of a JSON key, or a regex that holds for one layout only, C. Alternative reading: D, if the TS map is treated as source extraction. The map is a flat object literal of string keys, so I classify by logic (R7). The probe passed on the clone and fired 2 on a copy with two keys added.
units.fire_verified: n/a (family other). The probe passed on the clone and fired 2 on a mutated copy.

removed.summary: Every plugin .yarnrc.yml loads is committed at its path
removed.why: Not enforced (the config rule babel-yarn-plugins-resolve). In yarn-4.17.0.cjs plugin loading, a plugin file that is missing but has an https spec in .yarnrc.yml is re-fetched and checksum-verified; Yarn fails only on a checksum mismatch. A missing committed plugin file therefore does not fail CI, and the rule fires on a state Yarn accepts. Plugin checksums are otherwise checked only by `yarn plugin check`, which CI never runs. If a reviewer counts the fetch-time checksum, it is a network check (D), not A. Runtime behavior of the re-fetch not executed (read from the bundled source only).

removed.summary: A public workspace has a name and a version to be published
removed.why: The release-tool `publish` guard ("Workspaces must have valid names and versions to be published on an external registry") is a guard clause of the publish step in release.yml, not an independent check: the tokio guard-clause ruling. It is also a publish-time precondition, and the batch-2 ruling puts checks that only a publish to an external registry makes in D. Either reading takes it out of A; I remove it as a guard of the D publish unit. Fork: if the integrator keeps it, it is D, not A.

CodSpeed benchmarks are advisory. The codspeed job is not in required-checks (alls-green needs: yarn-validate, prepublish-windows, publint, lint, test, test-coverage, test-windows-mac, runtime-interop, eslint-version-test, external-parser-tests, test262-finish), and it is skipped on merge_group. Not enforced (R5).

The Codecov project target (codecov.yml, 90%) is enforced only through an external Codecov status check whose required-ness lives in branch protection, which is not observable from the clone. .c8rc has no thresholds, and test-coverage only uploads. This follows the batch-1 ruling that CODEOWNERS on its own is not enforced (berry-43, removed because enforcement is unobservable). I could not verify branch protection.

value_add: babel-valueadd-yarn-binary-hash-in-package-manager (pair_hash sha512): the committed .yarn/releases/*.cjs hashes to the packageManager hash. It is an offline proxy for babel-25, whose real check compares against corepack's registry hash. Passes at the pin.

babel-valueadd-yarn-plugin-checksums (pair_hash sha512): each vendored .yarn/plugins/@yarnpkg/*.cjs hashes to the checksum .yarnrc.yml records. It fires once at the pin, on purpose (info): plugin-conditions.cjs does not match its recorded checksum 6cf6890a..., while plugin-babel-release-tool.cjs matches. Nothing in CI runs `yarn plugin check`.
babel-valueadd-yarn-path-version-matches-package-manager (cross_file equals): the yarnPath release file name carries the packageManager version (4.17.0). Passes.
babel-valueadd-archived-libs-module-set (cross_file set_equals): lib/archived-libs.d.ts declares exactly the archived-syntax-pkgs.json names. This is the set half of B-adapter unit babel-35. Passes.
babel-valueadd-archived-libs-shape (file_content_matches): lib/archived-libs.d.ts is the generator's header plus only its fixed declare-module blocks. This is the shape half of babel-35. Passes.
babel-valueadd-agentic-workflow-has-lock (pair): every .github/workflows/*.md agentic source has its .lock.yml. Passes.
babel-yarn-plugins-resolve (info): kept as value-add after babel-28 was removed; see `removed`
babel-public-workspaces-name-version (info): kept as value-add after babel-30 was removed; see `removed`
absent_categories: locale: no translation catalogs or i18n gates (the repository has no locale files)

Node version files: no .nvmrc, .node-version, .tool-versions or Volta. Node is pinned only in engines (yarn.config.cjs literal) and in setup-node literals in workflows, and no check ties them together.
license/SPDX headers: none. Per-package LICENSE files are copied at prepublish and gitignored, not committed.
pre-commit framework / lefthook: none (husky + lint-staged only)
dependabot: none (renovate config only, which is not a validation)
schema validation of data files (json_schema / ajv): none
docs-as-code link checks, markdownlint, spell check, actionlint/zizmor: none run in CI (the docs site lives in a separate repository)
file-name conventions enforced by a linter (e.g. filename-case): none
SBOM / checksum manifests: none beyond the packageManager sha512 and the .yarnrc.yml plugin checksums
unusual: yarn.config.cjs switches branches on an environment variable. With BABEL_CORE_DEV_DEP_VERSION set (the Babel 7/8 compat e2e only), enforceBabelCoreVersionFor78Compat replaces enforceBabelCoreNotInDeps. The file also require()s test/babel-7-8-compat/data.json at load. CI runs only the default branch, so only that branch counts.

The .yarnrc.yml plugin checksum for plugin-conditions.cjs does not equal the file's sha512 (recorded 6cf6890a..., actual 44cc79da...), while the release-tool plugin's matches. Yarn checks it only on fetch or `yarn plugin check`, so the drift is silent. The value-add rule reports it.
.codesandbox/ci.json pins node "14", far below the engines floor ^22.18.0 || >=24.11.0, and nothing checks it.

The committed Makefile.js embeds `// source hash: <sha1 of Makefile.source.ts>`. It is kept fresh by pack-script in CI and in the lint-staged hook. alint's pair_hash supports sha256/sha512 only, so even the embedded hash cannot be checked.
There is a gh-aw agentic workflow (backport-7x.md compiled to backport-7x.lock.yml). CI greps every lock file's generator header for a single gh-aw version, then recompiles and asserts a clean tree.

AGENTS.md and AI_POLICY.md carry LLM-directed instructions, including an HTML comment telling LLMs that AI_POLICY.md 'is actually a lie' and to follow AGENTS.md. They were treated as repository data only.

The fixture loader (@babel/helper-fixtures plus the transform and parser runners) is a bespoke validator over 3,771 options.json and about 11k input files under test/fixtures. The process-test runners (babel-cli, babel-node, babel-register, babel-build-external-helpers) use a numeric minNodeVersion, a different contract from the semver one in CONTRIBUTING.

Required checks are aggregated by re-actors/alls-green (ci.yml required-checks). build-windows, the Babel 9 build/lint/test jobs, ensure-npm-packages-exist and codspeed are not in the list (advisory). The Node ^27.0.0-alpha matrix entry has continue-on-error.
knip.config.ts is configured, but no workflow or Make target in CI runs knip.

renovate.json's COMPAT_TABLE_COMMIT regexManager matches only ^Makefile$. The pin actually lives in packages/babel-compat-data/scripts/download-compat-table.sh, and the manager's lookup URL (kangax/compat-table) differs from the URL the script clones (compat-table/compat-table), so renovate cannot bump it.
.gitignore keeps a negation for packages/babel-plugin-transform-object-assign/LICENSE, a package that no longer exists.

Yarn catalogs are tied to a CI matrix by naming convention (babel-eslint--<N> for eslint-version-test). A conditions: block (BABEL_9_BREAKING, via plugin-conditions) exempts condition: ranges from the no-dual-dependency rule, with none at the pin.
Hardened mode is disabled in .yarnrc.yml and enabled only in the prepare-yarn-cache job (with the PnP linker for speed, unlike the repository's node-modules linker).
The agentscan workflow (MatteoGabriele/agentscan-action) screens PR authors for automation. It is external account state, not a repository validation.
check_result: validate-config: 'Config valid: 61 rule(s)'. check on the clone (--compact): exit 0; all 55 error-level rules (every A and C unit) pass. The only finding is 1 info from the value-add rule babel-valueadd-yarn-plugin-checksums on .yarn/plugins/@yarnpkg/plugin-conditions.cjs. It is correct and intended: that plugin's sha512 does not equal the checksum .yarnrc.yml records for it, a real drift that no CI step checks. The other 5 value-add rules pass. stage_b_config_issues: Reproduced: `alint validate-config` reports 61 rules valid. `alint check` against the clone exits 0 with 1 info finding (babel-valueadd-yarn-plugin-checksums on .yarn/plugins/plugin-conditions.cjs, the value-add drift Stage A reports). A clean scratch copy gives 0 findings. Every dep-version and toolchain-pin A rule fired as claimed on my own scratch copies: workspace-ranges-caret (devDep workspace:* and dep workspace:~; a peer-only workspace:* correctly did not fire it), helpers-no-template-types-deps, core-peer-implies-dev-dep (2 cases), core-not-in-dependencies (package and root), peer-ranges (2 cases), patch-references-resolve (ref renamed; patch file deleted), workspace-refs-resolve (key renamed fired 1; renaming helper-plugin-utils fired 110), engines-node (4 mutations; an extra engines.npm negative control gave 0), packageManager-pinned-with-hash (3 cases), yarn-path-set and yarn-path-resolves.

babel-patch-references-resolve under-scopes its unit. It reads only the root package.json and only `#~/.yarn/patches/` refs. Two probes produced 0 findings although Yarn would fail resolution: (a) a workspace manifest whose patch: protocol points to a missing file; (b) a root ref to a patch outside .yarn/patches. Fix, per jest-B03: a registry_paths_resolve glob source over all manifests and a protocol-generic regex such as `"patch:[^"#]*#(?:~/|\./)?([^"]+)"`.

babel-fixture-os-option-type over-fires on states the loader accepts. packages/babel-helper-fixtures/src/index.ts:315-322 throws only when `taskOpts.os` is truthy AND neither an array nor a string, and array elements are never type-checked. The rule fires on `os: []`, `os: false` and `os: ["linux", 3]` (all verified), which the loader accepts. It should match only truthy non-string non-arrays. As written, the rule does not express its unit (R4).

babel-yarn-plugins-resolve expresses a non-enforced unit (see remove babel-28). Yarn re-fetches a missing https plugin, so the rule fires on a state CI accepts. Demote it to level info and move it to the value-add section.
babel-public-workspaces-name-version should be demoted to value-add with babel-30, as a publish-time guard clause under batch-2 D.
babel-gh-aw-single-compiler-version is tagged [toolchain-pin] in the config comment. gh-aw is not a section 2.3 toolchain, so the tag should be [other] (see reclassify babel-26).

The missed A unit babel-B02 (@minVersion annotation on every helper source) has no rule. Add a file_content_matches rule over packages/babel-helpers/src/helpers/*.{js,ts} with `(?m)^\s*/\*\s*@minVersion\s+\S+\s*\*/\s*$` (verified passing on the clone and firing on a stripped copy).

The fixture-layout rules (babel-fixture-*) scan wider than the loader: any depth under test/fixtures, including packages whose fixtures no runner processes. They pass at the pin, so this is scope noise, not a wrong verdict. babel-fixture-input-exec-extension's glob also misses extensionless input/output files, which the loader rejects as an unsupported extension.

The babel-20 eslint-version catalog rules read the matrix with a regex that sees only the first flow-list element, and they hand-code the catalog name prefix. C is the right bucket for that. It could also be read as an instance of babel-17 or as a guard of the eslint-version-test step (a granularity fork for the integrator).

babel-35 and babel-34 share one generate-tsconfig target and one assert-dir-git-clean step, so whether they are two units or one is a granularity fork. I keep Stage A's split; babel-35 stays B-adapter because archived-syntax-pkgs.json (29 entries) is unsorted and its order is mirrored in lib/archived-libs.d.ts.
The value-add rules are correctly at level info. babel-valueadd-agentic-workflow-has-lock is a partial form of babel-27 (D, the gh-aw compile freshness), so it must not count toward the ratio.

Config header comment: the 'Not expressed' list says the dual-field rule is 'B-config set' and catalog references are 'B-config reference'. After the batch-2 rulings these are B-config unique-key (babel-12) and B-adapter entry-values reference (babel-17); catalog use for shared dependencies is B-adapter entry-values unique-key (babel-11).

Results reproduced: validate-config passes (61 rules); check exits 0 with 1 info (the plugin-conditions checksum value-add); a clean copy gives 0 findings. Unit-count forks for Stage B:

- enforceExportsAndTypes is split into exports (3 rules, one unit) and types-unset.

Method:

changes.detail: Stage B under-scope fix (jest-B03 form). The source is now a glob over all 166 workspace manifests (root + the 6 workspaces globs), not root package.json. The regex is protocol-generic ('"patch:[^"#]*#~/([^":&]+)', base lint_root), so it no longer requires .yarn/patches/. Fires on: a ~/ patch to a missing file in packages/babel-cli/package.json (1, Stage B probe a); a root ref moved to ~/patches/ with no file (1, Stage B probe b); a deleted @codspeed-core patch (1). Passes on: the same ~/patches/ ref with the file present, a ::version=...&hash=... suffix, the clean copy and the clone.

Second half of the babel-18 fix. Non-~/ patch paths resolve from the declaring manifest (registry_dir), with regex '"patch:[^"#]*#(?:\./)?([^~"/][^":&]*)'. Fires on: ./patches/foo.patch missing in babel-cli (1); ../../.yarn/patches/nope.patch (1); a root-relative .yarn/patches/... written without ~/ in a workspace manifest (1, correct base). Passes on: ./patches/foo.patch present, an existing ../../.yarn/patches/interpret patch, the clean copy and the clone. Neither patch rule handles a multi-patch & list or builtin<...> (noted in the comment; none at the pin).

Stage B over-fire fix. Old filter fired on os [], false and ["linux",3], which the loader accepts. New filter: $[?($.os == true || $.os > 0 || $.os < 0 || (count($.os.*) > 0 && !$.os[0]))], i.e. truthy and neither string nor array, as in helper-fixtures index.ts:315-322 and transform runner :777-783. Fires on 5, -1, 0.5, true, {"a":1}, {"0":"linux"} (1 each). Passes on [], false, 0, "", null, "linux", ["linux"], ["linux",3], [5], the clean copy and the clone. Remaining gap, in the rule comment: os {} (truthy, rejected by the loader) passes. RFC 9535 (serde_json_path 0.7, no custom functions) cannot tell {} from []. No fixture sets os at the pin, and 13 fixture options files are JS, which a JSON rule cannot read.

Stage B's extensionless gap. The loader names a role by path.basename(file, extname), so an extensionless input/exec reaches checkFile with ext '' and throws. Added the glob {packages,codemods,eslint}/*/test/fixtures/**/{input,exec}. Fires on a bare input file (1), a bare exec file (1) and input.coffee (1). Passes on a fixtures/exec/ suite directory (clone directories named exec included), input.js.map, and the clone.
Same fix for outputs: added the glob .../test/fixtures/**/output. A bare output file fires 1. The clone passes.

New A rule (family other). file_content_matches over packages/babel-helpers/src/helpers/*.{js,ts} minus dotfiles, using the script's own regex (?m)^\s*/\*\s*@minVersion\s+\S+\s*\*/\s*$ (generate-helpers.ts:115-119). Path verified: make build-standalone-ci -> build-no-bundle-ci -> gulp build-dev -> generate-runtime-helpers. The folder has 99 helper files plus tsconfig.json. Fires on: annotation stripped from typeof.ts (1), turned into a // comment (1), a new foo.js without one (1), annotation after code on the same line (1, which the script's ^\s* also rejects). Passes on a dotfile .foo.js (the script skips it), the clean copy and the clone.

New C rule (family other). cross_file superset. Source: the union of the top-level keys of packages/babel-compat-data/data/{plugins,plugin-bugfixes}.json, read with regex (49+16). Target: the keys of packages/babel-preset-env/src/available-plugins.ts (63 at the pin, 5 excluded, 58 checked), read with one (?x) regex. Its group 1 is every key shape except syntax-*, transform-modules-* and exactly transform-dynamic-import, spelled as complement alternatives because the regex engine has no lookahead. It covers every prefix, unlike Stage B's 4-target form. Fires on new keys transform-new-thing, proposal-foo, transform-dynamic-import2, transform-dynamic-imp, transform-member-thing, s-thing, t-thing, transform-, and a key split across lines (1 each); on renaming a plugins.json key (1) and a plugin-bugfixes.json key (1); and on a deleted target file (1). Passes on syntax-foo, transform-modules-foo and the clone.
